shared_elements: shallow/low relief carving on a stone slab or pillar
figures placed on the upper portion of a broad flat face
simplified silhouette-style animal bodies with raised outlines
justification: Both are broad, flat-faced stone monoliths bearing low-relief animals rendered as simplified raised silhouettes with a smooth surrounding ground, and in each case the imagery sits in the upper zone leaving the lower part blank or plain. The decisive difference is density and organisation: A carries a single isolated quadruped on an otherwise bare face, while B is filled with a multi-register composition of three arched motifs, a fringed band, birds, a quadruped and a snake, so the compositional schemes do not correspond.
